user.title: Arbiter
user.description: Arbiter decides what a switch should be doing when several automations disagree. Start in advisory mode: it will watch and report without changing anything.

data.override_sources: Automations that count as a person

data_description.bypass_entity: While this is on, Arbiter stands down completely and touches nothing.
data_description.default_mode: Used for any switch that does not set its own.
data_description.override_timeout: How long a person's action outranks every schedule.
data_description.override_sources: Scene-button automations belong here: holding a wall switch is a person acting, even though an automation carries it out.
data_description.unknown_source_priority: An automation with no reason mapping still gets a weak say, so nothing is silently dropped.
data_description.ignore_unknown_sources: Turn on to drop unmapped automations entirely instead.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Arbiter is already set up. Add reasons and switches from its integration page.

data.override_sources: Automations that count as a person

basics.title: What is this reason?
basics.description: A reason is why some switches should be on (or off), for as long as it lasts.

data_description.name: Short and lower case, e.g. daily, guests, holiday.
data_description.priority: Higher wins. Leave room between levels so you can slot new reasons in later.
data_description.lifetime: A window opens and closes on a schedule. A latch is opened by one automation and closed by another.

membership.title: Which switches
membership.description: Pick the switches this reason applies to. A label or area is usually better than a list, because it stays right when you add a switch later.

latch.title: How long it may stay open
latch.description: A latch is closed by another automation, which may not run on a given day. This bound is what stops a missed close from pinning the switches indefinitely.

data_description.entity_id: An input_datetime, or a sensor holding a timestamp such as a calendar-derived time.

end_kind.title: When does it end?
end_kind.description: The end is specified independently of the start, so an on-schedule and an off-schedule can come from completely different sources.

data_description.weekdays: Applies to the day the window starts on. Leave empty for every day.
data_description.condition: Re-checked when the entities it reads change.

data_description.mode: Advisory watches and reports. Guard also reverts whatever loses. Claims assumes your automations call arbiter.open and arbiter.close directly.
data_description.default_state: Choose 'unmanaged' to leave the switch alone when nothing is claiming it.

user.title: Map an automation to a reason
user.description: When this automation runs, does it open a reason or close one? An automation that turns things off at the end of an event almost always closes: closing lets whatever else is still live keep the switches on.

abort.no_reasons: Add at least one reason first — a mapping has to point at something.

options.claims: Claims — Arbiter is the only writer

options.window: A window — starts and ends on a schedule
options.latch: A latch — one automation opens it, another closes it

open.name: Open reason
open.description: Open a reason, so the switches it covers are held until it closes or expires.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Close it automatically after this long.

until.name: Until
until.description: Close it automatically at this time.

close.name: Close reason
close.description: Close a reason. The switches fall back to whatever else is still live, or to their fallback state.

override.name: Override
override.description: Hold a switch the way a person just set it, outranking every schedule.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Defaults to the configured override timeout.

clear_overrides.name: Clear overrides
clear_overrides.description: Drop manual overrides and let the schedules take back over.

entity_id.name: Switches
entity_id.description: Leave empty to clear every override.

set_mode.name: Set mode
set_mode.description: Change how far Arbiter may go for a switch.

explain.name: Explain
explain.description: Return the live reasons for each switch, which one is winning and why.

entity_id.name: Switches
entity_id.description: Leave empty for every managed switch.

find_conflicts.name: Find conflicts
find_conflicts.description: List every automation that can command each managed switch, which ones are switched off, which ones have no reason mapping, and what has actually fought.

export_config.name: Export configuration
export_config.description: Return the current configuration as YAML, for version control.
